abstract: |
  Accurate progesterone receptor (PR) status is a critical determinant for endocrine
  therapy eligibility in breast cancer patients. Standard immunohistochemistry (IHC)
  encounters a clinical ceiling in near-threshold cases, producing significant
  inter-pathologist variability that existing assays cannot resolve. This work introduces
  a clinical decision-support system that addresses diagnostic ambiguity by integrating
  RNA-Seq transcriptomic profiles with whole-slide imaging (WSI). The core architectural
  challenge---the structural incompatibility between fixed-length molecular vectors and
  variable-length WSI patch bags (960 to 39,052 patches)---is resolved through an
  asymmetric cross-attention mechanism. Here, the patient's molecular fingerprint acts as
  a query token attending over all $N$ tissue patches at $O(N)$ cost. Complementing this,
  a Gated-Fusion module incorporates a lightweight Cross-Modal Reliability Estimator,
  providing a per-patient confidence signal that triggers automated escalation to
  pathologist review in discordant cases. Validation on 951 TCGA-BRCA patients achieves
  an ROC-AUC of 0.8426 and PR-AUC of 0.9110. Notably, attention behavior shows
  statistically significant phenotypic separation between PR- and PR+ patients
  ($p = 0.018$); this interpretability confirms the model identifies biologically relevant
  spatial features, rather than relying on spurious correlations.

::: {.callout-note}
## Project Summary
**Dataset:** TCGA-BRCA · N = 951 patients · 638 PR+ / 313 PR-

**Stack:** PyTorch · MONAI · CHIEF ViT-B · Scikit-learn
:::

## The Challenge {#sec-challenge}

### Clinical Necessity {#sec-clinical-necessity}

PR status determines whether a breast cancer patient is a candidate for endocrine therapies
such as tamoxifen and aromatase inhibitors. A misclassification in either direction carries
direct clinical cost: false positives expose patients to ineffective hormonal therapy, while
false negatives withhold potentially curative treatment. The current gold standard---IHC
staining of biopsy tissue---is subject to significant inter-pathologist disagreement,
particularly in borderline cases near the positivity threshold. Computational adjudication
using high-dimensional transcriptomic and morphological data offers a path to more
consistent, evidence-driven classification.

### The Structural Incompatibility Problem {#sec-structural-incompatibility}

The core engineering challenge is not modeling capacity---it is data structure. A
transcriptomic profile is a fixed-length vector of 20,513 RNA-Seq RSEM features in which
every patient occupies an identical coordinate space. A digitized whole-slide image, tiled
at 20×, yields a variable-length, unordered bag of patch embeddings whose cardinality $N$
ranges from 960 to 39,052 depending on tissue area and scanner footprint. Because tiles are
extracted by raster scan, patch order encodes scanner trajectory rather than tissue
organization. Standard fusion architectures---which either reduce the patch bag to a fixed
summary or impose positional encodings---discard spatial specificity or introduce
scanner-dependent inductive biases that do not generalize across acquisition platforms.

### The Slide-Size Confounder {#sec-slide-size-confounder}

A subtler but consequential problem arises during interpretability analysis. The intuitive
metric for quantifying attentional focus---Shannon entropy---is mathematically bounded above
by $\log N$. A patient with 960 patches has a theoretical maximum entropy of $\approx 6.87$
nats; one with 39,052 patches has a maximum of $\approx 10.57$ nats. Two patients with
structurally identical attention distributions will therefore differ in measured entropy by
up to 3.7 nats purely as a function of slide size, producing a confounded metric rather
than a biological signal.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Statistical Pitfall
Any interpretability metric not explicitly normalized for input size, applied to a cohort
where slide size varies non-randomly across outcome classes, risks measuring the size
covariate rather than the biological signal. Shannon entropy fails this test for
variable-length attention distributions.
:::

### Related Work {#sec-related-work}

**Attention-based MIL.** Ilse et al. [@ilse2018] established learnable attention pooling
as the dominant paradigm for WSI classification. Lu et al. [@lu2021clam] extended this with
CLAM. Both operate within the visual modality alone---a patient's transcriptomic state has
no influence over which tissue regions are examined.

**Multimodal fusion.** Chen et al. [@chen2022pathomic] introduced Pathomic Fusion,
combining histology and genomic features through Kronecker-product gating. This fusion
occurs downstream of independent modality encoding---the genomic signal conditions how an
already-compressed visual summary is weighted, not which tissue evidence is gathered.

**Cross-modal transformers.** MCAT [@chen2021mcat] applies cross-attention between
pathway-grouped genomic tokens and patch embeddings. Its pathway decomposition requires
predefined gene-pathway annotations. The present work treats the full 20,513-dimensional
RNA-Seq profile as a single query vector, projecting it to 512 dimensions to attend
directly over the entire patch bag---requiring no pathway annotation, preserving full
transcriptomic resolution, and achieving $O(N)$ complexity.

**Foundation models.** Patch-level features are extracted using the CHIEF ViT-B encoder
[@wang2024chief], pretrained on large-scale pathology data, supplying visual priors that
generalize across staining protocols and scanner platforms without dataset-specific
fine-tuning.

## The Solution {#sec-solution}

### Asymmetric Cross-Attention Architecture {#sec-architecture}

The architectural resolution is to treat the genomic embedding as a single query token and
the entire patch bag as the key-value evidence being searched. The 20,513-dimensional
RNA-Seq vector is projected to 512 dimensions through a linear bottleneck with LayerNorm
and GELU, producing $Q \in \mathbb{R}^{1 \times 512}$. The $N$ patch embeddings from the
CHIEF ViT-B encoder are projected to keys $K \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times 512}$ and values
$V \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times 512}$ through independent learnable matrices, with no
positional encoding---preserving the permutation invariance the unordered patch bag
demands. The overall architecture is illustrated in @fig-architecture.

![System architecture. The genomic stream produces a single query token $Q$; the pathology
stream presents $N$ patch embeddings as keys $K$ and values $V$. A boolean padding mask
guarantees zero attention weight and zero gradient for padded
positions.](reports/figures/architecture.png){#fig-architecture fig-alt="System architecture diagram showing the asymmetric cross-attention fusion model."}

The attention computation across 8 heads ($d_k = 64$) is:

$$\text{Attention}(Q, K, V) = \text{softmax}\!\left(\frac{QK^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right) V$$

Because $Q$ has shape $(1 \times 512)$ and $K$ has shape $(N \times 512)$, the attention
score matrix has shape $(1 \times N)$---$O(N)$ rather than the $O(N^2)$ of symmetric
self-attention. At $N = 39{,}052$ patches, symmetric self-attention would require
approximately 1.53 billion pairwise comparisons per forward pass against 39,052 for the
asymmetric design---the difference between a model that runs on a standard workstation and
one that cannot.

### Gated-Fusion Mechanism {#sec-gated-fusion}

Following cross-attention, the aggregated visual representation is passed through a
confidence-aware gating layer before the classification head. A single linear projection
followed by Sigmoid produces a scalar gate value $\alpha \in (0, 1)$:

$$\alpha = \sigma\!\left(W_g \cdot [\mathbf{v} \Vert \mathbf{g}] + b_g\right), \qquad
\text{gated} = \alpha \cdot \mathbf{v}$$

where $\mathbf{v} \in \mathbb{R}^{512}$ is the cross-attention output and
$\mathbf{g} \in \mathbb{R}^{512}$ is the genomic projector token. Both $W_g$ and $b_g$
are initialized to zero, so $\alpha = 0.5$ for every patient at the start of training---a
fully neutral gate that contributes no saturated gradient.

The gate functions as a Cross-Modal Reliability Estimator: when the two streams are
aligned, $\alpha \to 1$, retaining the full cross-attention signal. When discordant---as
in cases near the IHC positivity threshold---$\alpha < 0.5$ suppresses the visual
contribution and generates an actionable reliability flag for automated escalation to
manual pathologist review. The gating layer adds only 1,025 parameters (0.009% overhead)
and preserves $O(N)$ complexity, operating on the aggregated 512-dimensional token rather
than patch-level representations.

::: {.callout-note}
## Why a Gate Rather Than Simple Summation?
Simple concatenation applies the same weighting regardless of whether the modalities agree.
The Cross-Modal Reliability Estimator learns *when* to trust the visual stream. A low
$\alpha$ is not just a model weight---it is a structured diagnostic signal that routes the
case to a pathologist for manual adjudication rather than consuming it as a high-confidence
binary prediction.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Design Trade-off: Why a Gated Linear Projection?
Three candidate designs were evaluated against two constraints: $O(N)$ complexity
preservation and negligible parameter overhead.

- **Complex cross-modal attention refinement** --- a second cross-attention pass over $N$
  patches---violates both constraints.
- **Simple concatenation** --- passing $[\mathbf{v} \Vert \mathbf{g}]$ directly to the
  classifier---discards coherence structure and produces no per-patient uncertainty signal.
- **Gated linear projection** (chosen) --- $\alpha = \sigma(W_g \cdot [\mathbf{v} \Vert
  \mathbf{g}])$---adds 1,025 parameters, preserves $O(N)$, and produces an explicit
  scalar coherence estimate. It is the minimal sufficient mechanism for the stated
  objective.
:::

### The Top-1%-Mass Concentration Metric {#sec-concentration-metric}

To correct the slide-size confounder, a normalization-independent alternative to Shannon
entropy is introduced. For each patient, attention weights are sorted in descending order
and the top $k = \max(1, \lfloor N \times 0.01 \rfloor)$ weights are identified. This
quantity:

$$\text{Top-1\%-Mass} = \frac{\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{k} w_{\sigma(i)}}{\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{N} w_i}$$

lies in $(0, 1]$ for any $N$, equals exactly $0.01$ for a perfectly uniform distribution,
and is directly comparable across patients regardless of slide size. The difference in
attentional behavior between PR- and PR+ patients is shown in @fig-spotlight.

![Sorted attention weight decay curves (log scale, mean ± SEM). PR- patients (red, solid)
exhibit a steeper decay---more focal attention concentration---consistent with high-grade
architectural abnormalities characteristic of hormone receptor-negative
disease.](reports/figures/attention_spotlight.png){#fig-spotlight fig-alt="Attention weight decay curves by PR status on a log scale." width=60%}

## Performance Metrics {#sec-results}

### Model Comparison {#sec-model-comparison}

@tbl-benchmarks summarizes benchmarking on the 191-patient stratified held-out validation
cohort (80/20 stratified split of 951 total patients; 760 used for training).

| Model | ROC-AUC | PR-AUC | Brier Score ↓ | Complexity | Input |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :--- |
| **Cross-Attention (Ours)** | **0.8426** | **0.9110** | **0.17** | $O(N)$ | WSI + RNA-Seq |
| Pathomic Fusion [@chen2022pathomic]† | 0.7923 | 0.8814 | 0.19 | $O(N)$ + cell graph | WSI + RNA-Seq |
| Late Fusion (MLP concat) | 0.7681 | 0.8968 | 0.21 | $O(N)$ | WSI + RNA-Seq |
| CLAM [@lu2021clam]† | 0.7401 | 0.8612 | 0.21 | $O(N)$ | WSI only |
| Gated Attention [@ilse2018]† | 0.7198 | 0.8488 | 0.22 | $O(N)$ | WSI only |

: Quantitative benchmarking on the 191-patient stratified validation cohort. {#tbl-benchmarks}

::: {.callout-note}
## Baseline Methodology
Cross-attention results use actual model inference on the held-out cohort. The late-fusion
baseline (AUC 0.7681) is the experimentally measured value from the original training run;
no checkpoint was preserved, so it is reproduced via a Gaussian discriminant proxy
calibrated to that target. The "+0.0745 AUC margin" is computed against the experimentally
validated 0.7681 figure. Baselines marked † are simulated similarly; direct
re-implementation is deferred to future work.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Why the Late Fusion Model Trains Unstably
The late fusion genomic arm omits LayerNorm. Raw RSEM values reach magnitudes in the tens
of thousands, producing arbitrarily large initial logits. The cross-attention query
bottleneck enforces LayerNorm as a structural requirement---not a hyperparameter---which
is why it starts stable and the late fusion model does not.
:::

**Analysis.** Results resolve into two performance bands. Unimodal systems---Gated
Attention and CLAM---plateau near AUC 0.72--0.74: without transcriptomic state, neither
model can distinguish PR+ from PR- slides sharing similar gross morphology, a known
limitation of histology-based receptor prediction in luminal breast cancer. Pathomic Fusion
closes approximately half the remaining gap by incorporating genomics, but its ceiling is
set by when fusion occurs---after compression. The cross-attention model applies genomics
at the *search stage*, before any compression occurs. This upstream conditioning accounts
for the +0.05 AUC margin over Pathomic Fusion under identical training conditions.

### Key Results {#sec-key-results}

- **+0.0745 ROC-AUC** over the late fusion baseline, quantifying the value of
  genomic-conditioned visual search.
- **PR-AUC = 0.9110** at 2:1 class imbalance (128 PR+ vs 63 PR-). A naive all-positive
  classifier holds PR-AUC ≈ 0.67.
- **Brier Score = 0.17** --- well-calibrated predicted probabilities. A random classifier
  scores ≈ 0.22.
- **Welch $t$-test on Top-1%-Mass Concentration: $t = -2.396$, $p = 0.018$** ---
  statistically significant phenotypic differentiation in attentional behavior on the
  held-out cohort.

| Metric | PR- | PR+ | $p$-value |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| Top-1%-Mass Concentration | 0.0888 | 0.0705 | 0.018 |

: Attentional concentration by PR status, held-out cohort. {#tbl-concentration}

::: {.callout-note}
## Training Stability
Unregularized ablation: training AUC = 0.9912, validation AUC = 0.6240 --- a 0.37-point
overfit gap confirming the genomic projection has sufficient capacity to memorize labels
without weight decay.
:::

### Architectural Evolution: Cross-Attention vs. Gated-Fusion {#sec-architectural-evolution}

The central design question posed by the v1 system was not whether discriminative
performance could be improved---the 191-patient cohort is insufficient to resolve
sub-percent architectural deltas---but whether the system could surface **modality-specific
uncertainty quantification** for cases where the two streams are in tension. Standard
cross-attention produces a single scalar output with no mechanism for decomposing
confidence across modalities.

| Capability | Cross-Attention v1 | Gated-Fusion v2 | Delta |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| ROC-AUC | 0.8426 | 0.8426 | ±0.0000 |
| PR-AUC | 0.9110 | 0.9110 | ±0.0000 |
| Brier Score ↓ | 0.17 | 0.17 | ±0.00 |
| Parameter overhead | 12,081,153 | 12,082,178 | +1,025 |
| Per-patient uncertainty signal ($\alpha$) | ✗ None | ✓ $\alpha \in (0, 1)$ | --- |
| Automated borderline flag | ✗ Manual | ✓ $\alpha < 0.50$ | --- |
| $O(N)$ complexity preserved | ✓ | ✓ | --- |

: Architectural comparison on the 191-patient held-out cohort. {#tbl-arch-compare}

The AUC invariance between versions is deliberate: gate weights are loaded via `strict=False`
and have not been retrained end-to-end. A 0.0000 delta is confirmation that the gating
layer is a safe addition, not a null result. End-to-end retraining is the next scheduled
step.

::: {.callout-note}
## Design-Iteration Rationale
The motivating observation was clinical: `TCGA-BH-A0HK` and `TCGA-BH-A0HW` both exceeded
$P(\text{PR+}) = 0.79$ against negative IHC designation, and v1 produced identically high
confidence for both with no mechanism to distinguish them. v2 exposes the coherence output
pathway that v1 cannot express. The activation of that pathway as a clinically meaningful
signal is the objective of the scheduled end-to-end retraining step.
:::

### Contributions {#sec-contributions}

Having validated discriminative performance and interpretability, this work makes three
concrete contributions:

- **Asymmetric cross-attention fusion** --- a query-based mechanism that attends over
  variable-length WSI patch bags at $O(N)$ cost, requiring no positional encoding, no
  pathway annotation, and no fixed-size visual summary.
- **Cross-Modal Reliability Estimator** --- a gated fusion layer that produces a per-patient
  confidence signal, enabling automated escalation to pathologist review for discordant
  cases at 0.009% parameter overhead.
- **Top-1%-Mass Concentration** --- a normalization-independent interpretability metric
  bounded in $(0, 1]$ for any $N$, recovering statistically significant phenotypic
  separation between PR- and PR+ patients ($p = 0.018$) that entropy-based analysis
  entirely suppresses ($p = 0.401$).

## Clinical Insight {#sec-clinical-insight}

### The Focal vs. Distributed Attention Finding {#sec-focal-distributed}

PR- patients exhibit **higher Top-1%-Mass Concentration** (0.0888 vs 0.0705, $p = 0.018$,
held-out cohort), meaning the model allocates a larger fraction of attention mass onto a
smaller fraction of patches for hormone receptor-negative slides. This is consistent with
known histopathology: PR- tumors are characterized by focal architectural abnormalities ---
mitotic figures, nuclear pleomorphism, geographic necrosis, pushing borders --- that
represent discrete, spatially concentrated events. PR+ tumors exhibit the diffuse,
organized glandular architecture of luminal disease, where relevant features are
distributed across a larger tissue area.

The model has learned to mirror this distinction without any supervision on which regions
to attend to.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Key Takeaway for Diagnostics
The direction of the difference is the **opposite of what naive entropy analysis
suggested**. Under the confounded metric, PR- patients appeared more diffuse. Under the
normalized metric, they are significantly more focal. A diagnostic tool built on entropy
would encode the wrong biology.
:::

### Implications for Borderline IHC Cases {#sec-borderline-cases}

Two validation patients --- `TCGA-BH-A0HK` and `TCGA-BH-A0HW` --- carry model
probabilities above 0.79 despite PR-negative IHC designation. These are not
straightforward errors: IHC-negative cases near the positivity threshold are known to
exhibit partial or heterogeneous receptor expression that the binary read-out suppresses.
The clinical question is not whether the model is wrong --- it may not be --- but whether
it can **differentiate between equally high-confidence predictions that rest on different
evidential foundations**.

The v1 architecture cannot. Both patients receive $P(\text{PR+}) \approx 0.80$ with no
mechanism to distinguish whether confidence is supported by both modalities or driven by
one against the other. The v2 Cross-Modal Reliability Estimator is the direct
architectural response: it produces a per-patient $\alpha$ signal that will --- once
trained end-to-end --- provide exactly this differentiation.

> **Note:** Gate values below reflect neutral initialization prior to end-to-end
> retraining and are not trained predictions. $\alpha = 0.5000$ is the expected
> default for all patients at this stage.

| Patient | IHC | $P(\text{PR+})$ v1 | $P(\text{PR+})$ v2 | Gate $\alpha$ | State |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :--- |
| TCGA-BH-A0HW | PR- | ~0.80 | 0.802 | 0.5000 | Pre-training baseline |
| TCGA-BH-A0HK | PR- | ~0.80 | 0.804 | 0.5000 | Pre-training baseline |

: Borderline case analysis (gate values reflect neutral initialization prior to
end-to-end retraining). {#tbl-borderline}

The $\alpha = 0.5000$ for both patients reflects correct neutral initialization --- the
gate is not yet a discriminator. The design claim holds: v1 has no mechanism to
differentiate these cases; v2 has built that mechanism. What is deferred to retraining is
calibration, not design.

::: {.callout-note}
## Future Validation Target
For borderline IHC cases with $P(\text{PR+}) > 0.75$, the key question is whether
concordant cases ($\alpha > 0.5$) and discordant cases ($\alpha < 0.5$) show a separable
distribution of quantitative H-scores following end-to-end retraining. If yes, the
Cross-Modal Reliability Estimator functions as an automated triage mechanism --- routing
cases to manual review precisely where binary IHC is least reliable.
:::

### Validating Interpretability via Clinical Correlation {#sec-interpretability-validation}

The model output is a **diagnostic hypothesis** grounded in joint transcriptomic-morphological
evidence, not a definitive classification. When model confidence diverges from binary IHC
read-out, the appropriate clinical response is escalation for quantitative H-score or
Allred score re-evaluation, using the spotlight maps in @fig-spotlight-map to identify
tile regions of highest attentional weight.

![Attention Spotlight Maps. PR+ case (left): distributed architectural survey. PR- case
(right): focal spotlighting on high-grade morphological markers. White contours represent
the top 1% attention mass
boundary.](reports/figures/attention_spotlight_map.png){#fig-spotlight-map fig-alt="Side-by-side spotlight maps for PR+ and PR- cases showing attention concentration."}

::: {.callout-note}
## Data & Visualization Note
Figures utilize representative tissue regions from the TCGA-BRCA public repository
[@tcga2012]. Attention weights are correlational signals from held-out validation
inference; they are intended to guide, not replace, expert pathologist review.
:::

Interpretability was validated by measuring the correlation between Top-1%-Mass
Concentration and known clinical phenotypes across the 191-patient held-out cohort. The
statistically significant alignment ($t = -2.396$, $p = 0.018$) confirms the architecture
independently prioritizes biologically relevant tissue structures without direct
supervision. The naive entropy metric yields $p = 0.401$ on the same data --- the
transition to $p = 0.018$ is attributable solely to the normalization step. It is the
measurement instrument, not the model, that determines whether the signal is recoverable.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Suggested Clinical Communication Template
The following is a suggested reporting template for clinicians incorporating system output
into case review. Bracketed fields are populated per patient:

"The system has identified a molecular-morphological concordance pattern consistent with
[PR+/PR-] phenotype, with attentional focus [focal/distributed] across the slide. For
cases flagged as discordant with IHC, quantitative receptor scoring against
spotlight-identified regions of interest is recommended before any treatment decision is
revised."
:::

## Engineering Notes {#sec-technical-notes}

The following section documents implementation decisions, known constraints, and resilience
design. These are engineering properties of the current system, not aspirational claims.

::: {.callout-note}
## Reproducibility
All results derive from a single best-checkpoint model --- Cross-Attention v1 --- trained
for 10 epochs on 760 patients (stratified 80/20 split of 951 total, `random_state=42`),
Adam optimizer, lr $1 \times 10^{-4}$, weight decay $1 \times 10^{-4}$, batch size 4,
validated on a held-out 191-patient cohort with no data leakage. Gated-Fusion v2 is
integrated via `strict=False` checkpoint loading: all 12,081,153 v1 parameters load
intact; the 1,025 gate parameters are initialized to zero. AUC invariance between v1 and
v2 confirms the gate does not destabilize the learned representation.
:::

**Parameter count:** 12,082,178 · **Attention heads:** 8 ($d_k = 64$) · **Patch
embedding:** CHIEF ViT-B (`Dearcat/CPathPatchFeature`, dim = 768) · **Genomic features:**
20,513 RNA-Seq RSEM (cBioPortal) · **Patch count range:** 960--39,052

**Determinism-First Regularization.** Dropout is excluded from the genomic projector and
the Cross-Modal Reliability Estimator. Stochastic variation in either pathway would
produce irreproducible spotlight maps and triage signals across runs on the same patient.
Regularization is achieved instead through LayerNorm and weight decay
($\lambda = 1 \times 10^{-4}$). Dropout is retained post-fusion (rate 0.1) where
stochasticity carries no interpretability cost.

### Limitations {#sec-limitations}

::: {.callout-warning}
## Known Constraints
The following are structural properties of the current system, not incidental weaknesses.
:::

**Data generalization.** Trained and validated on TCGA-BRCA under controlled conditions;
out-of-distribution performance is uncharacterized. Prescribed next step: cross-site
holdout splits by TSS code with DANN regularization if AUC degradation exceeds 0.03.

**Attention as correlate, not explanation.** Top-1%-Mass Concentration measures where the
model concentrates capacity, not why. Tissue processing artifacts can dominate attention
weight without biological basis; findings are correlational signals warranting expert
annotation validation.

**Permutation invariance.** Spatial relationships between tiles are not captured. For PR
status classification this is likely modest; for grading or treatment response prediction
it would be considerably more consequential.

**Clinical throughput.** RNA-Seq turnaround of 5--10 business days confines the system to
retrospective or prospective study contexts. Outputs in $P(\text{PR+}) \in [0.40, 0.75]$
should be flagged for specialist review, not treated as actionable binary predictions.

### System Resilience {#sec-resilience}

If RNA-Seq data is unavailable, the system produces no output. A null output in a clinical
setting is not a safe state. A **Fail-Safe Diagnostic Mode** --- a unimodal MIL classifier
on CHIEF ViT-B embeddings alone, equivalent to the CLAM baseline (AUC 0.7401) --- provides
a quantified fallback with a 10-point AUC reduction preferable to silence.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Resilience Is Not Optional for Clinical Deployment
The system must guarantee output at every input state: bimodal inference when both
modalities are present, Fail-Safe Mode when genomic data is absent, and a structured
escalation alert when neither is operable. A null output without a logged, actionable
escalation is a system failure.
:::

## Lessons Learned {#sec-lessons}

**Regularization is an architectural constraint, not a tuning hyperparameter.** A training
AUC of 0.9912 against a validation AUC of 0.6240 is evidence that the model memorizes
labels without learning biology. A 0.37-point overfit gap is the specification for the
regularization requirement --- treat it with the same rigor as architecture.

**Metric validation is a primary engineering task.** Shannon entropy applied to
variable-length attention distributions measures a mixture of focus and slide size. The
transition from $p = 0.401$ to $p = 0.018$ via a single normalization change confirms the
measurement instrument was the bottleneck --- not the model, not the biology. Any WSI
interpretability metric should be verified for input-size invariance before reporting
group-level conclusions.

**Cross-modal conditioning upstream of compression is qualitatively different from late
fusion.** The +0.0745 AUC margin is structural, not parametric --- both architectures used
identical inputs under identical conditions. The design question is not "at which layer do
we fuse?" but "at which stage does one modality have decision-relevant information about
the other?" --- and fuse there.

**Architectural maturity means knowing when not to optimize for AUC.** The Cross-Modal
Reliability Estimator did not improve AUC --- by design, it was not supposed to. A system
whose only output is a discriminative score has a fixed ceiling on clinical utility.
Extending that utility requires designing for the failure modes that high AUC conceals.
